scope: Owner-authorized John Tanner, Eleazer Miller, and John Rowe Moyle history enrichment; existing heroes and original artwork preserved.

narrative_sources.label: Brigham Young: Our Search for Truth and Personal Testimony
Teaching by the Spirit: Miller identified in Brigham’s account
Dieter F. Uchtdorf: Lift Where You Stand

historical_boundaries: Tanner healing explicitly attributed to Jared Carter’s reported witness; debt forgiveness attributed to retrospective family history; no invented dialogue, medical diagnosis, or universal financial promise.

Canonical Eleazer Miller (1795–1876), not William Miller, Joseph Millett, or Artemus Millet. Omit uncertain precise conversion interval and baptism day; Brigham’s search involved study and personal choice.

John Rowe Moyle (1808–1889), not his similarly named son. Injury, weekly walk, and carved inscription attributed to Uchtdorf’s retelling. He died before the 1893 dedication. Disability is not a faith comparison.
Films identified as dramatizations; actors are not authenticated historical portraits. Scripture connections are invitations to reflection, not revelations addressed to these three men.

source_paraphrase_review: No verbatim quotations. Moyle paragraphs 2–3 derive approximately 128 words from Uchtdorf; biography/migration/death from CHD and remaining reflection original. Tanner separates Carter witness (~68 words), Kirtland account (~80), JSP biography (~40), and Arrington debt recollection (~40). Miller source-derived portions split among CHD, Brigham chapter 43, chapter 9 and Maxwell quotation; no single page reaches 200 words.
